task_context.problem_statement:
An industrial machine can make 3 shirts a minute. It made 4 shirts yesterday and 8 shirts today.
How many minutes did the machine work in all?
( ( 4.0 + 8.0 ) / 3.0 )

messages.content: I have to do this problem: An industrial machine can make 3 shirts a minute. It made 4 shirts yesterday and 8 shirts today. How many minutes did the machine work in all? I honestly don't even know where to start. I'm so bad at math, it's just frustrating.

It's completely normal to feel stuck when you first look at a word problem. We can take this one step at a time together. To start, let's just look at the total number of shirts. Based on the problem, how many shirts did the machine make in total over the two days?
I guess it's 4 from yesterday and 8 from today... so 12 shirts? But I probably messed that up already.

You didn't mess that up at all; 12 is exactly right. Now that we know the total number of shirts produced, how can we use the machine's speed (3 shirts per minute) to figure out the total time spent working?
I don't know. Do I multiply 12 by 3? No, that doesn't seem right. I always get the operations mixed up. I'm just wasting your time.

You aren't wasting my time, and mixing up operations is a very common part of learning. Think of it this way: if the machine makes 3 shirts every single minute, and it needs to make 12 shirts total, would it take more or less than 12 minutes? Would multiplying or dividing help you find how many 'groups of 3' are in 12?
Oh, if it's 3 per minute, it should take less time than 12 minutes. So I should divide 12 by 3. That would be 4?
That's correct! You walked through the logic perfectly. You found the total shirts and then divided by the rate to find the total minutes. Great job sticking with it.
